column26: Description

column1: Customer identity verification (DOB, post code, card digits)
column26:
* *User Story:* As a delinquent customer, I want to verify my identity on the web portal using my date of birth, post code and the last 4 digits of my registered payment card, so that I can securely access my overdue account details without waiting to speak with a representative.
* *Business Value:* Enables secure 24/7 self-service while protecting customer data (GDPR). No account details are shown until verification passes.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** When an unauthenticated customer opens the portal, the verification screen asks for Date of Birth, Post Code and last 4 digits of the registered payment card and shows no account details.
** When the customer submits all three fields, the portal validates them against the legacy database in real time.
** When all three match, the customer proceeds to the hardship check (KAN-16) and then the Account Dashboard (KAN-12).
** When any field does not match, a generic error is shown (it does not say which field was wrong), the customer can retry, and the failed-attempt count increases by one.
** Every verification attempt (pass or fail) is written to the audit log (KAN-26) without storing the answers entered.
** On the 3rd consecutive failed attempt the journey passes to KAN-14 (lockout and fallback); this story defines no lockout behaviour.
* *Dependencies:* Read access to the legacy database; Compliance confirmation of the verification standard (BLOCKER, see Notes); KAN-26 audit logging.
* *Priority:* Highest (Must-have): every other portal story needs a verified customer.
* *Estimate:* 5 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* Static fields, not dynamic knowledge-based questions. The identity verification standard is NOT yet confirmed by Compliance, so the fields and attempt limits may change before build. Owner to be confirmed (see Phase 1 scope assumptions).

column1: Account dashboard: overdue balance and repayment options
column26:
* *User Story:* As a verified customer without a hardship flag, I want to see my current overdue balance, account status and the ways I can resolve it on one dashboard, so that I know what I owe and what I can do next.
* *Business Value:* Gives customers transparency about what they owe and removes the need to phone for 'what do I owe / what was agreed' follow-ups. Baseline to validate: the Finance stakeholder reports customers call back about three times after a first call; the figure must be checked against the Discovery Dossier and recovery activity tracker before it is quoted in the ROI case.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** When a verified customer with no hardship flag (KAN-16) reaches the dashboard, it shows total overdue balance (GBP), product type (Personal Loan / Credit Card / Auto Finance), days overdue and current account status.
** Balance and status are read live from the legacy database; if they cannot be read, an error message and the support number are shown instead of stale data.
** The dashboard offers: Pay Overdue Balance in Full (KAN-20), Set Up Repayment Plan (KAN-18), Promise to Pay (KAN-19), Request Hardship Support / Dispute Balance (KAN-21) and View Transaction History (KAN-17).
** Options that the account is not eligible for (KAN-22) are not displayed.
* *Dependencies:* KAN-11 (verification); KAN-16 (hardship check); legacy database read access.
* *Priority:* Highest (Must-have): entry point to every resolution journey.
* *Estimate:* 5 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* Hardship-flag behaviour is owned by KAN-16 and is not repeated here. The earlier 'specialist callback form' is out of Phase 1 unless confirmed by Compliance.

column1: Failed verification lockout and fallback to representative
column26:
* *User Story:* As a Compliance Liaison, I want the portal to lock access after 3 failed verification attempts and show a support number, so that customer data is protected from unauthorised access while genuine customers still have a route to help.
* *Business Value:* Prevents credential guessing while giving struggling customers a human fallback.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** When verification fails 3 consecutive times for an account, portal login for that account is locked for 60 minutes.
** At the same time the portal displays the representative support telephone number.
** The case is placed in the representative queue for manual identity verification (KAN-27).
** A locked customer who tries again sees the lock message and the support number, and no further attempts are accepted.
** The lock lifts automatically after 60 minutes, or earlier when a representative resets it in the admin queue; both are written to the audit log (KAN-26).
* *Dependencies:* KAN-11, KAN-26, KAN-27.
* *Priority:* High (Must-have): security control required before go-live.
* *Estimate:* 3 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* This is the single owner of lockout behaviour; KAN-11 only hands over to it. Lock and phone-number display happen together, as in the To-Be workflow. The 60-minute duration is to be confirmed with Compliance.

* *User Story:* As a Compliance Liaison, I want customer sessions to end automatically after 5 minutes of inactivity, so that sensitive financial details are protected if a device is left unattended.
* *Business Value:* Meets banking security expectations and reduces data-exposure risk.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** When an authenticated customer is inactive for 4 minutes, a modal shows 'Session will timeout in 60 secs' with a countdown.
** Any customer activity while the modal is showing dismisses it and restarts the inactivity timer.
** When 5 minutes pass without activity, the session is cleared, no account data remains on screen, and the customer is returned to the verification screen.
* *Dependencies:* KAN-11.
* *Priority:* High (Must-have): small, security-driven.
* *Estimate:* 3 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* Applies to every authenticated screen. Assumption to confirm: a payment already submitted to the gateway is not interrupted by a timeout.

* *User Story:* As a Collections Representative, I want accounts with an active hardship or vulnerability flag to be diverted from self-service after login, so that vulnerable customers receive personal, compliant support.
* *Business Value:* Protects vulnerable customers and keeps the bank compliant with vulnerable-customer rules.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** After successful verification, the portal checks the account's hardship/vulnerability flag in the legacy database before showing the dashboard.
** If the flag is set, no payment, plan or promise-to-pay options are shown, and the message 'Your account requires personal support. Contact a specialist team member on this number.' is displayed with the number.
** The account is placed in the specialist representative queue with the reason 'pre-existing hardship flag' (KAN-23).
** If no flag is set, the customer proceeds to the dashboard (KAN-12).
** The flag check result is written to the audit log (KAN-26).
* *Dependencies:* KAN-11, KAN-23, KAN-26; hardship flags already set during intake screening.
* *Priority:* Highest (Must-have): compliance requirement; the workflow places this check before any account data is shown.
* *Estimate:* 3 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* Single owner of pre-existing flag behaviour; KAN-12 and KAN-21 refer to this story instead of repeating it. Customer-initiated hardship requests are KAN-21.

* *User Story:* As a verified customer, I want to view my recent payments, so that I can confirm my payment progress without a paper statement or email.
* *Business Value:* Replaces payment-confirmation emails (out of Phase 1 scope) with self-service visibility.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** When the customer selects View Transaction History, a table lists transactions newest first with date, amount, payment type (Card / Direct Debit) and remaining balance.
** The table covers up to 12 months of records.
** If there are no transactions, the message 'No payments recorded in the last 12 months' is shown.
** A payment made through the portal appears once it has been written to the database (KAN-25).
* *Dependencies:* KAN-12, KAN-25.
* *Priority:* Medium (Should-have): the on-screen receipt in KAN-20 is the primary confirmation, so this can follow the core journeys.
* *Estimate:* 5 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* 'Direct Debit' appears as a payment type only once KAN-28 ships.

* *User Story:* As an overdue customer, I want to choose a 3-, 6- or 12-month repayment plan online, so that I can clear my balance on terms I can afford without negotiating by phone.
* *Business Value:* Increases recovery through affordable plans and saves representative call time on straightforward cases.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** Plan options are shown only for accounts flagged portal eligible (KAN-22) with a balance under the automatic-acceptance threshold (value to be confirmed).
** When the customer selects a duration of 3, 6 or 12 months, the portal calculates and shows equal monthly payments and the total repayable before confirmation.
** When the customer confirms, the first instalment is taken through the payment gateway using the capability and failure handling in KAN-20.
** On success, the plan is recorded as a 'repayment arrangement' in the legacy database (KAN-25) and an on-screen summary shows plan length, instalment amount and due dates.
** If the first payment fails, no plan is recorded and the customer is shown the failure message and alternatives.
* *Dependencies:* KAN-12, KAN-20, KAN-22, KAN-25; agreed policy threshold for automatic acceptance (open).
* *Priority:* High (Must-have): core value case, standard plans need no manual sign-off.
* *Estimate:* 5 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* The Direct Debit mandate for later instalments is split out to KAN-28 (Should-have). Until it ships, later instalments are paid by card via the portal and checked by KAN-29. Assumes no interest or fees; confirm.

* *User Story:* As an overdue customer unable to pay today, I want to set a payment promise date online, so that my account shows a commitment and I am not chased in the meantime.
* *Business Value:* Captures commitments electronically and stops unrecorded callback promises across shifts.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** When the customer selects Promise to Pay, they can choose a date from tomorrow up to 30 days ahead and enter an amount greater than 0 and no more than the overdue balance.
** On submit, an on-screen confirmation shows the promise date and amount.
** The account is recorded as 'PTP captured' with amount, promise date and UTC timestamp in the legacy database (KAN-25), and is visible to representatives.
** Promises are accepted automatically for accounts with no hardship or dispute flag.
* *Dependencies:* KAN-12, KAN-25; KAN-29 checks the promise when it falls due.
* *Priority:* High (Must-have): headline capability in the To-Be workflow.
* *Estimate:* 3 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* Maximum term is not agreed: this story says 30 days, an earlier scope draft said up to 6 months. Confirm with Collections Operations. Following up unpaid promises is KAN-29.

column1: One-off full card payment and on-screen receipt
column26:
* *User Story:* As an overdue customer, I want to pay my full overdue balance by card online, so that I can resolve my account immediately and see proof of payment.
* *Business Value:* Accelerates cash collection and removes manual payment handling by representatives.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** When the customer selects Pay Overdue Balance in Full, the full overdue amount is shown (not editable) and card details are entered securely before Submit Payment.
** The payment is processed through the payment gateway and card details are never stored by the portal.
** On success, an on-screen receipt shows a unique reference, amount and date, the overdue balance becomes 0.00 GBP, and the new status is written to the database (KAN-25).
** On a declined payment, a clear message is shown, the balance is unchanged, and the customer can retry with another card, choose another option, or see the support number.
** On a gateway timeout or error, the portal checks the transaction status before allowing a retry so the customer is not charged twice; unresolved cases show the support number and go to a representative (KAN-23).
* *Dependencies:* Payment gateway merchant account and integration (owner TBC); KAN-12, KAN-25.
* *Priority:* High (Must-have): fastest route to recovered cash; largest build item.
* *Estimate:* 8 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* Phase 1 supports full balance only. Part payments are handled through plans (KAN-18) or promises (KAN-19). Card payment only.

column1: Raise hardship or dispute request from portal
column26:
* *User Story:* As a customer in financial hardship or disputing my balance, I want to request specialist support on the portal, so that a representative has my details and I do not have to repeat my story.
* *Business Value:* Protects vulnerable customers and avoids representatives re-asking for information.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** When the customer selects Request Hardship Support or Dispute Balance, they choose the request type and answer a 3-question context form (questions to be approved by Compliance), then select Submit.
** On submit, self-service ends for the account and the customer sees a confirmation, what happens next, and the support number.
** The account is flagged for hardship or dispute in the legacy database (KAN-25).
** A priority case with the customer's answers is placed in the specialist representative queue (KAN-23).
** The submission is written to the audit log (KAN-26).
* *Dependencies:* KAN-12, KAN-23, KAN-25, KAN-26.
* *Priority:* High (Must-have): compliance and vulnerable-customer safeguard.
* *Estimate:* 5 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* Flags are accepted automatically; assessment of the claim is out of Phase 1. Accounts already flagged before login are handled by KAN-16.

* *User Story:* As a representative, I want accounts assessed against agreed eligibility rules when they become delinquent, so that straightforward cases use self-service and complex cases come to me.
* *Business Value:* Lets simple cases be resolved quickly while protecting specialist capacity.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** When an account enters delinquency, the system assesses it against the eligibility rules agreed with Collections and Compliance.
** The rules consider at least: hardship or vulnerability flag, open dispute, balance above the automatic-acceptance threshold and product type (illustrative; final list to be confirmed).
** An eligible account is flagged 'portal eligible' in the legacy database and the customer is notified how to access the portal (channel to be confirmed).
** An ineligible account is not flagged and is routed to the representative queue with the reason (KAN-23).
** The outcome and the rule that decided it are written to the audit log (KAN-26).
* *Dependencies:* Approved eligibility rules (BLOCKER); account data in the legacy database; KAN-23, KAN-25, KAN-26.
* *Priority:* Highest (Must-have): first step of the To-Be workflow; nothing else starts without it.
* *Estimate:* 5 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* Included in Phase 1 scope (rules-based triage). The one-off access notice is separate from the payment-confirmation emails excluded from scope.

* *User Story:* As a representative, I want complex, hardship and failed cases routed to me with context, so that I can give appropriate support without starting from scratch.
* *Business Value:* Makes sure cases that need a human reach the right team.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** When triage (KAN-22), the hardship check (KAN-16), a hardship/dispute request (KAN-21), failed verification (KAN-14/KAN-27), a write-back failure (KAN-30) or an unpaid promise (KAN-29) needs a person, the account is removed from self-service.
** The case appears in the standard or specialist queue with account ID, reason code, timestamp and any customer-entered context.
** The escalation reason is stored against the account in the legacy database.
* *Dependencies:* KAN-22, KAN-16, KAN-21, KAN-14, KAN-29, KAN-30; queue tooling available to representatives.
* *Priority:* High (Must-have): the safety net behind every exception path.
* *Estimate:* 3 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* Queue response-time targets (SLA) are not defined yet; confirm with Collections Operations.

column1: Escalate unresolved payments to a manager
column26:
* *User Story:* As a representative, I want unpaid or unresolved cases escalated to a manager when necessary, so that they receive appropriate follow-up.
* *Business Value:* Prevents unresolved accounts being overlooked so more debt is recovered.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** When a promised or planned payment is not received (flagged by KAN-29), the case appears in my worklist with the reason 'payment not received'.
** I can record the follow-up outcome and, if unresolved, escalate to a manager with a reason.
** The escalation (who, when, why) is recorded against the account and in the audit log (KAN-26).
* *Dependencies:* KAN-29, KAN-23, KAN-26.
* *Priority:* Medium (Should-have): representatives can follow up manually until this exists.
* *Estimate:* 3 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* The legal review path after manager escalation is out of Phase 1 scope.

column1: Sync account status to legacy database
column26:
* *User Story:* As a representative, I want account status changes made on the portal written to the legacy database automatically, so that staff and customers see consistent information without re-keying.
* *Business Value:* Removes manual re-keying and improves data accuracy and compliance.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** When a payment is made, a plan is arranged, a promise is captured, a hardship or dispute request is raised, a portal-eligible flag is set or an account is settled, the new status is written to the legacy database with account ID and UTC timestamp.
** The write completes before the customer sees a final confirmation.
** The updated status is visible to representatives in existing tools and to the customer on the dashboard (KAN-12) on next load.
** A failed write is handled as described in KAN-30.
* *Dependencies:* Write access to the legacy database; KAN-30.
* *Priority:* Highest (Must-have): the legacy database is the source of truth, so most stories depend on this.
* *Estimate:* 5 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* Legacy database stays the source of truth.

column1: Record customer and system actions in audit trail
column26:
* *User Story:* As a compliance or management user, I want key customer and system actions recorded, so that there is a clear, tamper-resistant history of account activity.
* *Business Value:* Provides an audit trail and the data needed for later reporting and compliance checks.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** These events are recorded: verification attempts, lockouts and resets, manual ID verification, triage outcome, hardship flag check, payments, plan set-up, promise capture, hardship/dispute requests, escalations and write-back failures.
** Each record holds account ID, event type, UTC timestamp, actor (customer, system or representative ID) and outcome. Card details and answers entered are not stored.
** Records are append-only and cannot be edited or deleted by the portal or by staff.
** Compliance users can retrieve records by account ID and date range.
* *Dependencies:* Audit table in the legacy database (existence to be confirmed; if missing, a schema change is needed).
* *Priority:* High (Must-have): compliance control and prerequisite for reporting.
* *Estimate:* 5 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* Management reporting dashboards are outside Phase 1; this story captures the data that would feed them.

* *User Story:* As a Collections Representative, I want to verify a locked-out customer's identity manually, so that genuine customers can still access help and fraudsters are stopped.
* *Business Value:* Gives genuine customers a path back into the journey after a lockout.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** When a lockout case (KAN-14) is in my queue, I can see the account and the failed-attempt history and verify the customer using data from the legacy database.
** I record the verification attempt and outcome in the legacy database.
** If verified, the portal lock is reset so the customer can continue to the hardship check (KAN-16) and dashboard.
** If not verified, the case is escalated to a manager and recorded.
** Every step is written to the audit log (KAN-26).
* *Dependencies:* KAN-14, KAN-23, KAN-26.
* *Priority:* High (Must-have): the To-Be workflow shows this fallback after failed verification.
* *Estimate:* 5 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* Manual checks follow the same Compliance verification standard as KAN-11.

column1: Set up Direct Debit mandate for repayment plan
column26:
* *User Story:* As a customer on a repayment plan, I want to set up a Direct Debit online, so that my remaining instalments are paid automatically.
* *Business Value:* Improves plan completion and reduces missed payments.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** After a plan is confirmed (KAN-18), the portal shows a Direct Debit mandate form (account holder name, sort code, account number).
** Bank details are format-validated before submission.
** On submit, the mandate is processed and an on-screen confirmation with mandate reference is shown, and the reference is recorded in the legacy database (KAN-25).
** If the mandate fails, the customer sees an error and can retry or pay instalments by card.
* *Dependencies:* KAN-18, KAN-25; Direct Debit provider or gateway support (owner TBC).
* *Priority:* Medium (Should-have): a heavier build than card payment, so it can follow the core release.
* *Estimate:* 8 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* Split from the original KAN-18. Not part of the Phase 1 core if the provider is not ready.

column1: Automated payment monitoring for promises and plans
column26:
* *User Story:* As a Collections Representative, I want the system to check automatically whether promised and planned payments have arrived, so that I do not have to remember to check manually.
* *Business Value:* Improves follow-up consistency and cuts manual checking effort.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** When a promise date or plan instalment due date arrives, the system checks the payment status in the legacy database without staff action.
** If paid, the status is updated to 'payment settled' or 'instalment received' (KAN-25) and no representative action is needed.
** If not paid, the account is flagged and routed to the representative queue with the reason 'payment not received' (KAN-23).
** Each check and its result is written to the audit log (KAN-26).
* *Dependencies:* KAN-18, KAN-19, KAN-23, KAN-25, KAN-26; a scheduling capability in the portal environment (to be confirmed).
* *Priority:* High (Must-have): the To-Be workflow depends on this check after the promise timer.
* *Estimate:* 5 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* Grace period before flagging (for example 1 day) is to be confirmed. Added after review: KAN-19 and KAN-24 previously relied on this with no story.

* *User Story:* As a Collections Representative, I want failed status updates to the legacy database retried and flagged, so that the portal and the source of truth never silently disagree.
* *Business Value:* Protects data integrity, which the portal depends on because the legacy database is the source of truth.
* *Acceptance Criteria:*
** When a write to the legacy database fails, the portal tries the update again automatically before reporting a failure (number of attempts to be confirmed).
** If all retries fail, the customer sees a neutral message that the request has been received and is being confirmed, with the support number; the portal does not claim a status that was not saved.
** The failed update is kept and a task with the full details goes to the representative queue for reconciliation (KAN-23).
** The failure and its resolution are recorded in the audit log (KAN-26).
* *Dependencies:* KAN-25, KAN-23, KAN-26; a named operational owner for failed write-backs (OPEN: none assigned today).
* *Priority:* High (Must-have): payments may already be taken when a write fails.
* *Estimate:* 5 story points
* *Notes & Assumptions:* The scope document notes there is no owner if write-back fails; one must be named before build.
